application: Access card / test card / legacy stored-value card
summary: A widely used memory card family with sectors, blocks and Crypto-1 authentication.

memoryLayout.sectorTrailer: Each sector has data blocks and a sector trailer containing Key A, access bits and Key B.

security.notes: Legacy security. Many systems rely on keys and access bits.

magicCardSupport: Possible with compatible magic/test cards when legally authorized.
safeRecommendedActions: Make a full backup only for cards you own or are authorized to test
Use Sector Explorer after a dump is available
Compare future dumps to track changes
beginnerExplanation: MIFARE Classic cards store data in sectors and blocks. To understand one properly, first identify it, then create a legal backup, then inspect the sectors.

cardProfile.name: MIFARE Classic
cardProfile.description: MIFARE Classic is an HF memory-card family with sectors and blocks. Public scan data can identify the card, while sector contents usually require valid keys.
normallyAbsentData: person name unless an application stored it
NFC Forum NDEF unless formatted that way
limitations: Sector contents require valid authorized keys
UID alone does not explain the application
Legacy security means deployments vary widely
recommendedNextSteps: Use authorized keys before reading sectors
Compare future dumps if you own the card
cardProfile.meaning: This card can contain structured data in sectors. Without valid keys, Electron can identify the family but cannot explain protected sector contents.
notVisibleReasons: Protected sectors require authentication with valid keys.
Names, expiry dates or balances only appear if the issuer application stored them on-card.
Some systems store real-world meaning in a backend database instead of on the card.

faqs.question: Why can Electron identify the card but not read all contents?
faqs.answer: MIFARE Classic uses sector keys. Identification is public, but sector data is protected until a valid authorized key is available.

faqs.question: Does UID tell me what the card is used for?
faqs.answer: Not by itself. UID identifies the physical card; the application meaning depends on stored sector data or a backend system.
